paper.title: Contrarian Investment, Extrapolation, and Risk
paper.citation: Lakonishok, Josef, Andrei Shleifer, and Robert W. Vishny (1994), Journal of Finance / NBER Working Paper No. 4360, May 1993.

definition.value: Weighted average of a stock's annual sales-growth rank over the five pre-formation years (years -1 through -5), with more recent years given greater weight; deciles formed on this weighted-average rank define the GS (growth-in-sales) strategy.

evidence.location: Section III, paragraph beginning "An alternative way to get at glamour and value..." (p.12-13)
evidence.quote: our classification of stocks into GS dediles is based on average rank of their sales growth, rather than the raw growth number... For each company, we then compute its weighted average rank, giving the weight of 5 to its growth rank in year -I, the weight of 4 to its growth rank in year -2, etc. Finally, we form deciles based on each stock's weighted average growth of sales rank.

economic_intuition.value: Past sales growth proxies for whether a stock is glamour (high past growth, extrapolated to continue) or value (low past growth, out of favor); ranking-then-weighting smooths year-to-year sales-growth noise while still weighting recent growth more heavily.

evidence.location: Section III, paragraph beginning "An alternative way to get at glamour and value..." (p.12)
evidence.quote: The extrapolation story, as well as the evidence discussed above, suggests that stocks with high past growth are typically glamour stocks, and stocks with low past growth are out-of-favor or value stocks. We measure past growth by growth in sales, GS, which is less volatile and less often negative than either growth in cash flow or growth in earnings

On average, over the S post-formation years, the low oS strategy earns an abnormal return of 2.2 percent, and the high GS strategy earns the abnormal return of -2.4 percent. ... The value strategy outperforms the glamour strategy, on average, in each of the 5 post-formation years.
evidence.interpretation: Low weighted-average sales-growth-rank decile (value) earns higher subsequent size-adjusted return than the high decile (glamour), so the signal-return relation is negative.

formula.paper_expression: For each stock, compute annual sales growth in each of years -1 through -5 relative to formation; cross-sectionally rank stocks by sales growth separately within each of the five years; take the weighted average of those five annual ranks, weighting year -1 by 5, year -2 by 4, year -3 by 3, year -4 by 2, and year -5 by 1; sort stocks into deciles on this weighted-average rank.

steps.description: Compute each firm's sales growth for each of the five pre-formation years, using the paper's portfolio-based ($1-invested) growth-rate procedure.
steps.expression: sales_growth_year_k = sales_year_k / sales_year_{k-1} - 1, for k in {-1, -2, -3, -4, -5}

evidence.location: Section II, Methodology, paragraph beginning "Let us illustrate our procedure for computing growth rates..." (p.7)
evidence.quote: To compute the growth of sales in year -3 relative to formation, we consider a portfolio that invests $1 in each stock, and look at the sales generated by this portfolio in years -4 and -3, and use the percentage change as our growth measure.
evidence.interpretation: The paper's headline growth-rate procedure is described generically here; the GS-strategy paragraph (Section III) confirms the same year -1...-5 sales-growth measure is used for the ranking input.

steps.description: Rank all eligible stocks by that year's sales growth, separately for each of the five pre-formation years.

evidence.location: Section III, paragraph beginning "An alternative way to get at glamour and value..." (p.12-13)
evidence.quote: Specifically, for each company for each of years -1, -2, ..., -5 prior to formation we calculated the growth of sales in that year. Then, for each year, we rank all companies by growth in sales for that year.

steps.description: Weighted average of the five annual ranks, with the most recent year weighted most heavily (weights 5,4,3,2,1 for years -1,...,-5).

evidence.location: Section III, paragraph beginning "An alternative way to get at glamour and value..." (p.13)
evidence.quote: For each company, we then compute its weighted average rank, giving the weight of 5 to its growth rank in year -I, the weight of 4 to its growth rank in year -2, etc.

notes: Manually re-derived (no LLM extraction call) directly from the paper text cache, for comparison against runs/method_specs/raw/Contrarian investment, extrapolation, and risk.pdf__MeanRankRevGrowth.raw.json. Targets the paper's simple univariate GS (growth-in-sales) strategy reported in Table 4 -- the pre-formation 5-year weighted average rank of annual sales growth, weights 5,4,3,2,1 for years -1...-5. The paper also reports BM (Table 1), CP (Table 2), EP (Table 3), and several bivariate strategies (GS x CP in Table 5, EP x GS in Table 6, BM x GS in Table 7); none of those are merged into this single-signal target. One addition vs. the existing raw file: a third reported_results metric (gs_value_minus_glamour_cab5, the cumulative 5-year size-adjusted spread of 22.7%) that is stated directly in Section III text rather than read off a table cell.
